jobs.title: Director Advanced Analytics and AI
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

Our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) team within Operations helps turn high-value opportunities into practical solutions that improve how work gets done across the business. As the Director, AI Delivery, you'll lead the end-to-end delivery of a growing portfolio of AI and Generative AI initiatives, from opportunity identification and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and value realization. You'll lead and develop a team of data scientists while creating the structure, operating rhythm, and accountability needed to deliver consistently in a complex enterprise environment. Working closely with Operations leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll translate business problems into clear, well-scoped initiatives with measurable outcomes. You'll also manage competing priorities across the portfolio, remove barriers to progress, and help ensure solutions are successfully embedded into business workflows. Success in this role means building a delivery organization that scales effectively, delivers predictably, and creates measurable business impact.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How You'll Succeed

Lead delivery excellence - Own the end-to-end delivery of the Operations AI portfolio, from intake and prioritization through development, production, adoption, and realized value. Create clear ownership, execution discipline, and accountability across initiatives.
Build trusted business partnerships - Partner closely with Operations leaders and teams to understand business needs, identify high-value AI opportunities, and shape a sustainable pipeline of use cases with clear outcomes and success measures.
Manage the portfolio - Continuously assess and prioritize concurrent AI initiatives based on business value, feasibility, capacity, dependencies, and evolving insights. Make pragmatic decisions on scope, sequencing, resourcing, and delivery approach to maintain momentum.
Navigate enterprise delivery - Drive initiatives forward with partners across data science, engineering, technology, risk, governance, and the business. Anticipate blockers and dependencies early, and work across the organization to resolve them.
Embed solutions for impact - Ensure AI solutions don't stop at production and are effectively adopted into business workflows to achieve intended outcomes. Create transparency into delivery progress, risks, capacity, portfolio health, and business value.
Develop your team - Lead, coach, and support a team of data scientists across multiple levels of experience. Help team members build ownership, strengthen stakeholder management, and increase delivery effectiveness over time.

Who You Are

You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and leading teams responsible for delivering complex technology or AI initiatives. You create clarity and accountability while empowering talented people to take ownership of their work.
You can demonstrate experience in delivering Generative AI solutions in a business environment, portfolio delivery, and cross-functional execution across business and technology teams. It’s an asset if you also bring broader experience in artificial intelligence and machine learning delivery.
You give meaning to data. You understand enough about AI and Generative AI delivery to challenge assumptions, identify delivery risks, and work effectively with data scientists and engineers. You balance technical understanding with strong business judgment.
Your influence makes a difference. You're comfortable working directly with senior business leaders and building trusted relationships across diverse partner groups. You can challenge priorities, scope, and expectations in a constructive and effective way.
You act like an owner. You focus on business outcomes, adoption, and value realization rather than activity alone. You make thoughtful trade-offs, know when to accelerate or reshape work, and can stop initiatives that aren't delivering enough value.
Values matter to you. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.
You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.
We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency).
We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

Job Location

Toronto-81 Bay, 21st Floor

Employment Type

Regular

Weekly Hours

37.5

Skills

Agentic AI, Applications Delivery, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Business Development, Customer Success, Customer Success Management (CSM), Delivery Focused, Generative AI, Generative AI Agents, Project Delivery, Talent Management, Technical Management

jobs.title: Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
Working at the City of St. Albert means joining a dedicated team that aims to deliver outstanding service to our vibrant community. We pride ourselves on employing a diverse group of employees who each bring unique skills and contribute to delivering exceptional services to our residents. We value collaboration, accountability, respect, and enjoyment in our work each day.

Job Details

Reporting to the Managing Director, Corporate and Emergency Services / Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Information Technology provides strategic and operational leadership for the City’s information technology function and the Information Technology Department.

The Director is accountable for departmental performance, people, financial and resource management, and the delivery of secure, reliable, resilient, cost-effective and continuously improving enterprise technology and information management services. They ensure that technology strategies, investments, systems, projects, and service improvements align with Council priorities, corporate objectives, operational and service delivery requirements, regulatory obligations, and governance standards. As the City’s senior advisor on technology, cybersecurity, information management and digital transformation, the Director works with City leadership to establish enterprise technology strategy, governance and priorities, manages the technology portfolio, and advises Executive Leadership and Council on significant technology opportunities, risks and decisions.

Working across the organization, the Director strengthens collaboration between IT and business areas, ensures technology services and investments deliver value, respond to business needs, manage organizational risk, enable innovation and modernization, and support effective municipal service delivery.

Responsibilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the City's Information Technology Department, ensuring secure, reliable, resilient and cost-effective technology and information management services.
Establish and lead enterprise technology, information management and digital transformation strategies, priorities and long-term plans.
Provide strategic advice to Executive Leadership and Council on technology, cybersecurity, information management, business continuity, digital transformation and emerging technologies.
Oversee the City's technology investment and project portfolio, including major technology acquisitions, implementations and modernization initiatives.
Direct departmental operations, workforce planning, budgeting, resource allocation and service delivery, while fostering a high-performing, accountable and customer-focused culture.
Build strong relationships across the organization to ensure technology services, investments and priorities align with business needs, corporate objectives and effective municipal service delivery.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, or a related discipline from a recognized post-secondary institution is required. A Master's degree is preferred.
At least 10 years of progressively senior information technology experience, managing and/or directing an IT operation, including five or more years managing a major IT operation in a municipal, public sector, or recognized consulting environment.
A Diploma in computer science, information systems, or other related discipline from a recognized post-secondary institution may be considered with 15 years of related experience.
Professional certifications in project management, organizational change management, IT governance, management consulting, or IT service management are considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience with technology governance, portfolio management, investment prioritization and major project delivery.
Broad knowledge of enterprise technology, including infrastructure, cloud services, enterprise applications, networks, cybersecurity, data and information management, service management, business continuity and disaster recovery.
Strong executive leadership skills with demonstrated ability to lead managers, professional and technical teams.

Hours of Work

This position works 40 hours per week, Monday – Friday (8:00 – 5:00) and receives 1 Earned Day Off (EDO) per month.
Benefit from flexible work hours by adjusting your start and end times by 30 or 60 minutes around our business hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Compensation

The salary ranges from $164,477.56 - $198,426.54 per year, including a comprehensive benefits package with a flexible spending account, pension plan, supplementary pension, monthly vehicle allowance and accrued paid vacation starting at 5 weeks per year.
Learn more about our benefits here: Employee Benefit Guide.

Why You Should Work With Us

This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. While most employees within the department work remotely, the Director will maintain a hybrid presence to support leadership, collaboration, and operational needs. Employees are eligible to participate in this program after 3 months of employment, subject to satisfactory performance.
You will receive a Flexible Spending Account limit at the beginning of each calendar year (permanent full time $400).
Employees can purchase an annual Recreation Access Pass for $87 + tax, granting unlimited access to Servus Credit Union Place (excluding PLAYcare and registered programs), Fountain Park Recreation Centre, and Grosvenor Outdoor Pool.
Free parking near most City worksites (ask for location specific details).

Conditions of Employment

The successful candidate will be required to provide proof of educational and professional credentials.
The successful applicant will be required to obtain a satisfactory police information check.
Please note that the presence of charges or convictions does not automatically preclude an individual from being considered for employment. All findings will be reviewed and assessed in relation to the responsibilities and requirements of the position.
A valid Alberta Class 5 Driver’s Licence and access to a personal vehicle for business use are required.

Application Information

Click 'apply' and you will be taken to the City of St. Albert Careers website www.stalbert.ca/employment.
Please upload both a cover letter and resume as part of your application. These documents must be submitted as separate attachments.
This competition will close at 10:00 p.m. MDT on October 29, 2026.

jobs.title: Finance & Human Resources Leader
jobs.description:
Location: Kingsville, Ontario
Vacancy: This posting is for a currently open position.
Salary Range: $130,000 – $150,000 base salary

COMPANY PROFILE

Our client is a fast-growing Canadian manufacturer of custom conveyor systems, material handling solutions, and precision metal products that has doubled their business in the past 2 years. They credit this success in large part to talented professionals who make up their world-class manufacturing team. They are committed to sustaining this period of growth, investing in the people, equipment, process improvements, and technology the business needs to scale effectively.

As the company enters its next phase of growth, it is establishing a new Finance & Human Resources Leader position. The Finance function has been overseen by the President & CEO and is now being transitioned to a dedicated leader who will assume full ownership of Finance, join the senior leadership team, and build on a strong existing foundation. With a capable team already managing the day-to-day finance and administrative activities, the focus will be on providing strategic leadership, strengthening the function, and supporting the company’s continued growth.

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to the General Manager, the Finance & Human Resources Leader will lead the Finance function while providing oversight of Human Resources. This is a key leadership role responsible for financial reporting, planning, controls, and performance analysis, with a strong focus on manufacturing operations. The successful candidate will bring financial insight to business decisions, strengthen processes and reporting, and serve as a trusted partner to the General Manager and leadership team. The role also provides HR direction and oversight, supported by internal resources and external partners as needed- the individual does not need to be an HR specialist.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Finance & Financial Leadership

Lead the Finance function, overseeing financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, working capital, and overall financial performance.
Prepare and communicate financial statements, management reporting, and analysis, providing actionable insights to the President & CEO and leadership team.
Oversee core financial operations, including AR, AP, payroll, banking, tax, audit, insurance and compliance, while maintaining strong financial controls and processes.
Provide financial oversight for capital expenditures and key business decisions, assessing risks, opportunities, and financial impact.

Manufacturing Finance

Develop a strong understanding of the company’s engineer-to-order manufacturing model and its key financial drivers.
Provide visibility into job costing, WIP, project margins and profitability, analyzing estimated versus actual performance across labour, materials and overhead.
Establish meaningful financial and operational KPIs and partner with Estimating, Sales, Engineering and Operations to translate operational performance into actionable financial insights.
Identify opportunities to improve margins, profitability, efficiency and working-capital management.

Human Resources

Provide leadership and oversight of the Human Resources function, ensuring policies and practices support business objectives, company culture and employment legislation.
Partner with managers on employee relations, performance management, recruitment, onboarding, retention, succession planning, compensation and benefits.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Serve as a trusted business partner to the President & CEO and an active member of the leadership team, contributing to strategic and organizational priorities.
Strengthen financial and HR systems, processes and reporting while identifying opportunities to automate repetitive work and leverage technology and AI to improve efficiency and decision-making.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Minimum 7 years of progressively senior experience in finance and accounting, ideally within a manufacturing environment; CPA designation is an asset.
Background in custom manufacturing, engineer-to-order, project-based, or similarly complex production settings.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, WIP, gross margin analysis, project profitability, and budget-to-actual performance.
Proven experience managing financial planning, forecasting, reporting, P&L oversight and cash flow management.
Strong knowledge of accounting practices, financial controls and governance, with experience improving financial processes and infrastructure.
Previous exposure to HR leadership or functional oversight, with an understanding of employee practices, policies and employment compliance.
Business-oriented and analytical, with the ability to connect financial and operational data to sound, practical business decisions.
Confident communicator and approachable leader who can build strong relationships across the organization, from senior leadership to front-line employees.
Proactive, hands-on, and continuous improvement-focused, with an openness to using technology, automation, and AI to enhance business efficiency.

If you’re a hands-on finance leader looking to shape both the financial and people side of a growing manufacturing business, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact. Please send your resume to lead executive search consultant Charles Warren
by selecting the “Apply” option and following the required steps.

Thank you in advance for your interest, only individuals deemed to have the skill set and experience to fit the role will be contacted. Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada without sponsorship.

jobs.title: Sales Director - Digital Transformation
jobs.description:
IBS is a leading global provider of new generation IT solutions to Travel, Transportation and Logistics industries since 1997. IBS provides a broad range of industry leading products and services that manage mission critical operations of airlines, airports, cruise lines, hospitality partners, tour operators and oil & gas companies. These products improve safety, revenue and workflow efficiency, while manage growth, and reducing operating costs.
At IBS, we provide mission critical B2B and B2C enterprise SaaS solutions to 170 of the world’s largest global travel brands including: American Airlines, LATAM, Avianca, Air Canada, British Airways, Lufthansa, Qantas, Caesars Entertainment, Disney, Starwood, IHG, Expedia, Booking & Priceline, just to name a few.
Our goal is to continue our successful 26-year track record. We will accomplish our goal by designing and delivering world class, game-changing products that provide our customers with unmatched business value, and the agility to compete in a dynamic and digital marketplace. To achieve this goal, we will continue to seek out exceptionally talented and motivated individuals to join our organization.
We are currently searching the market for an experienced, dynamic, organized, self-starter to join as Sales Director/Account Manager for our Consulting and Digital Transformation (CDx) line of business.
The Sales Director will nurture and grow new pipeline in the Airline, Hospitality and Travel space. Requires a good understanding of market and competition to develop appropriate sales strategies and apply the sales and solution expertise, in conjunction with project teams. Keen to get their hands dirty and actively helps the team develop value propositions based on a firm understanding of opportunity areas.
We are seeking a strong Hunter with good knowledge in Airline, Hospitality, Travel domain experience and consulting capability on digital transformation.

Responsibilities:

This role is 50% account management and 50% sales
Responsible for identifying and closing new deals in the consulting and digital transformation services
Work on building pipeline, defining marketing content and promoting them
Be the face of IBS to the market and help position IBS as an industry leader and trusted advisor for clients of focus
Leverage the IBS ecosystem of capabilities across digital innovation, domain experience and delivery excellence to develop solutions that address the client’s business problems
Strong in communication and storytelling and have a minimum of 3-5 years working in Digital transformation with a restless creative, innovative mindset and the ability to understand business and customer needs using the leading trends in the industry, market, and technology
Innovative mindset behind developing new platform solutions based on market research

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree or foreign equivalent required from an accredited institution.
10+ years of experience, with strong selling capability in consulting and digital transformation services
Understanding of Global Delivery Model and large deal experience
Track record of engaging and building relationship with senior leaders, CXOs of cient organization
Hands-on experience with proposal creation, crafting solutions and leading proposal presentation, marketing
Strong leadership, interpersonal, communication and presentation skills

Work Authorization

Canadian citizenship or permanent residency required. Must hold a valid passport.

Travel

This position requires 50% to 75% travel within the Americas Region (North America and South America). Most of the business trips are 2 to 3 days in length, with overnight stays.

At IBS you can look forward to:

Working with the latest next generation technologies and architected platforms
Operating with the brightest minds in the industry
Gaining additional in-depth domain knowledge
Receiving global exposure
Benefiting from continuous learning programs
Functioning out of state-of-the-art facilities and infrastructure
Performance-based career growth
Joining an excellent work culture
Competitive compensation, company paid employee benefits, vacation, sick and personal leave, company matched 401K

IBS is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status or any other characteristic protected by law. IBS as an equal opportunity employer bases its hiring decisions on the business need and the best-qualified candidates available, and does not discriminate in its employment decisions based on any protected category. Candidates offered employment may be subject to a criminal record and other background checks as permitted or required by company policy or applicable law.

jobs.description:

Toronto, ON

The successful placement within the range will depend on qualifications, relevant work experience, and other applicable considerations.

Why join us?

The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future. We are charged with purpose
, delivering reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity for homes, businesses, and communities across the province. We are energized to grow
, embracing opportunities to shape the future of a dynamic and evolving energy sector while advancing our careers. We are powered by teamwork
, supported by diverse and passionate colleagues who foster respect, celebrate successes, and thrive on shared achievements. At the IESO, it’s not just what we do— it’s who we are!

Who We Are

Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.

This is a non-unionized position that falls within the Corporate Relations, Engagement and Strategy business unit.

What Makes This Role Exciting

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the organization's strategic direction and drive initiatives that have enterprise-wide impact. Working closely with senior leaders, the role influences corporate strategy, oversees its implementation, and leads high-profile CEO and organizational priorities. The position offers a rare combination of strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and people leadership, allowing you to see ideas progress from concept to measurable results.

For someone who enjoys solving complex challenges and creating organizational alignment, this role sits at the center of the organization's most important priorities.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you’ll make a meaningful impact by contributing to the IESO team and supporting the electricity needs of the province through:

Leading the development and socialization of the Corporate Strategy, working in close partnership with Directors and senior leaders. Coordinate strategic planning activities, stakeholder engagement, and supporting research, and develop recommendations for Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and Board consideration and approval.
Leading the development of the Strategy Implementation Plan, including prioritization of strategic initiatives, milestones, performance measures, and implementation approaches. Facilitate engagement with business areas and provide recommendations to support ELT decision-making and approval.
Overseeing enterprise-wide monitoring, measurement, and reporting of progress against strategic objectives. Establish and implement reporting approaches, assess organizational performance against strategic commitments, identify emerging risks and issues, and provide insights and recommendations to support leadership decision-making.
Coordinating and aligning corporate strategy activities with other enterprise planning functions, including business planning, enterprise risk management, enterprise change, procurement, workforce planning, etc. Identify opportunities to strengthen the Enterprise Planning Framework and recommend improvements that enhance organizational alignment and execution.
Leading the delivery of CEO-sponsored and strategic initiatives, such as ESG framework, organizational alignment reviews, and other corporate priorities. Direct supporting research, analysis, and project activities; oversee external consultants and contractors where required; and develop recommendations arising from initiative outcomes for consideration by the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
Provide leadership, direction, and coaching to team members, ensuring the effective delivery of corporate strategy, strategy implementation planning, enterprise reporting, and strategic initiatives through clear priorities, performance expectations, and professional development support.

Decision-Making Responsibilities

Contribute to developing the approach, methodology, and stakeholder engagement process for the development of the Corporate Strategy and Strategy Implementation Plan.
Approve research, analysis, and other work products supporting strategy development, implementation planning, and strategic initiatives.
Determine the approach for strategy performance oversight and enterprise reporting.
Lead the selection and management of consultants and contractors supporting strategy or strategic initiative work, in accordance with organizational policies and procurement requirements.
Make decisions related to the coordination, prioritization, and execution of strategic and CEO-sponsored initiatives.

Recommendations

Recommend the Corporate Strategy, developed in collaboration with Directors and key stakeholders, for consideration and approval by the Executive Leadership Team and Board.
Recommend the Strategy Implementation Plan, including strategic priorities, sequencing of work, performance measures, and resource considerations, for Executive Leadership Team approval.
Recommend enhancements to the Enterprise Planning Framework to strengthen alignment across corporate strategy, business planning, enterprise risk management, enterprise change, workforce planning, procurement, and other enterprise functions.
Develop and present recommendations arising from CEO-sponsored and strategic initiatives, including opportunities, risks, implementation approaches, and organizational impacts, for consideration and approval by the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations to senior leadership on organizational performance, emerging issues, risks, trends, and opportunities identified through strategy oversight, reporting, and environmental scanning activities.

Role Requirements

Our team consists of experts from diverse backgrounds, each bringing their unique perspectives and skills.

To Succeed In This Role, You’ll Need

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Public Policy, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
12-15+ years of progressively senior experience in government relations, public affairs, strategy, policy, or a related function, preferably within the electricity or broader energy sector.
Strong knowledge of the electricity sector, government and regulatory environments, strategic planning and execution, business operations, and financial and budget management.
Proven ability to influence and build relationships with senior leaders, and other internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to convey complex issues effectively and drive alignment.
Demonstrated success leading, developing, and motivating professional teams while fostering collaboration and delivering strategic outcomes.

How We Support You

From a comprehensive total rewards program to dynamic learning and development opportunities—including job rotations to broaden your expertise—we empower you to define and shape your own success. When you join the IESO, here’s what you can expect:

Best-in-class benefits and long-term support in the form of a defined benefit pension plan.
Work in a dynamic and evolving sector that offers exciting opportunities and the chance to explore new career paths.
Leadership that values meaningful discussions, welcomes feedback, and prioritizes career development.
A strong, inclusive culture and a collaborative team environment with a shared passion for impactful work.
Compensation packages that are regularly reviewed to remain competitive and to best accommodate the diverse needs of our employees.

Deadline

October 29, 2026. For future reference, please save a copy of the job posting as it will no longer be available once the posting closes.

Thank you for your interest in a career at the IESO. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Please note that the successful candidate must be legally eligible to work in Canada and will be subject to applicable background checks.

IESO will not conduct interviews or offer positions via online, text, chat or social media platforms. We will not gather personal information directly from candidates or potential candidates. Selected candidates will work with our Talent Acquisition team to ensure their application is processed.

The IESO currently has a 3-day in-office work week for applicable roles. Over the course of 2026, the IESO will advance plans to acquire additional office space to accommodate more in-office time. While the timeline for moving to a full 5-day in-office model has not yet been established, we are committed to keeping employees and candidates informed as plans progress and give them as much advance notice as possible to prepare for any changes.

We believe in opportunities for everyone.

At the IESO, we know that achieving great results depends on embracing diversity by attracting, developing, and retaining people from a wide variety of backgrounds. We do this by ensuring our recruitment and advancement policies are fair and equitable, and by creating an accessible and inclusive environment—one that values every team member’s unique skills and experiences and ensures they have the support they need to achieve their potential. If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please let us know. We’re proud to say we’ve been recognized as a supportive, inclusive employer.

Be sure to follow us on LinkedIn

new_jobs.title: Finance & Human Resources Leader
new_jobs.description:
Location: Kingsville, Ontario
Vacancy: This posting is for a currently open position.
Salary Range: $130,000 – $150,000 base salary

COMPANY PROFILE

Our client is a fast-growing Canadian manufacturer of custom conveyor systems, material handling solutions, and precision metal products that has doubled their business in the past 2 years. They credit this success in large part to talented professionals who make up their world-class manufacturing team. They are committed to sustaining this period of growth, investing in the people, equipment, process improvements, and technology the business needs to scale effectively.

As the company enters its next phase of growth, it is establishing a new Finance & Human Resources Leader position. The Finance function has been overseen by the President & CEO and is now being transitioned to a dedicated leader who will assume full ownership of Finance, join the senior leadership team, and build on a strong existing foundation. With a capable team already managing the day-to-day finance and administrative activities, the focus will be on providing strategic leadership, strengthening the function, and supporting the company’s continued growth.

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to the General Manager, the Finance & Human Resources Leader will lead the Finance function while providing oversight of Human Resources. This is a key leadership role responsible for financial reporting, planning, controls, and performance analysis, with a strong focus on manufacturing operations. The successful candidate will bring financial insight to business decisions, strengthen processes and reporting, and serve as a trusted partner to the General Manager and leadership team. The role also provides HR direction and oversight, supported by internal resources and external partners as needed- the individual does not need to be an HR specialist.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Finance & Financial Leadership

Lead the Finance function, overseeing financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow, working capital, and overall financial performance.
Prepare and communicate financial statements, management reporting, and analysis, providing actionable insights to the President & CEO and leadership team.
Oversee core financial operations, including AR, AP, payroll, banking, tax, audit, insurance and compliance, while maintaining strong financial controls and processes.
Provide financial oversight for capital expenditures and key business decisions, assessing risks, opportunities, and financial impact.

Manufacturing Finance

Develop a strong understanding of the company’s engineer-to-order manufacturing model and its key financial drivers.
Provide visibility into job costing, WIP, project margins and profitability, analyzing estimated versus actual performance across labour, materials and overhead.
Establish meaningful financial and operational KPIs and partner with Estimating, Sales, Engineering and Operations to translate operational performance into actionable financial insights.
Identify opportunities to improve margins, profitability, efficiency and working-capital management.

Human Resources

Provide leadership and oversight of the Human Resources function, ensuring policies and practices support business objectives, company culture and employment legislation.
Partner with managers on employee relations, performance management, recruitment, onboarding, retention, succession planning, compensation and benefits.

Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Serve as a trusted business partner to the President & CEO and an active member of the leadership team, contributing to strategic and organizational priorities.
Strengthen financial and HR systems, processes and reporting while identifying opportunities to automate repetitive work and leverage technology and AI to improve efficiency and decision-making.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Minimum 7 years of progressively senior experience in finance and accounting, ideally within a manufacturing environment; CPA designation is an asset.
Background in custom manufacturing, engineer-to-order, project-based, or similarly complex production settings.
Strong understanding of cost accounting, WIP, gross margin analysis, project profitability, and budget-to-actual performance.
Proven experience managing financial planning, forecasting, reporting, P&L oversight and cash flow management.
Strong knowledge of accounting practices, financial controls and governance, with experience improving financial processes and infrastructure.
Previous exposure to HR leadership or functional oversight, with an understanding of employee practices, policies and employment compliance.
Business-oriented and analytical, with the ability to connect financial and operational data to sound, practical business decisions.
Confident communicator and approachable leader who can build strong relationships across the organization, from senior leadership to front-line employees.
Proactive, hands-on, and continuous improvement-focused, with an openness to using technology, automation, and AI to enhance business efficiency.

If you’re a hands-on finance leader looking to shape both the financial and people side of a growing manufacturing business, this is an opportunity to make a lasting impact. Please send your resume to lead executive search consultant Charles Warren
by selecting the “Apply” option and following the required steps.

Thank you in advance for your interest, only individuals deemed to have the skill set and experience to fit the role will be contacted. Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada without sponsorship.

Why join us?

The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future. We are charged with purpose
, delivering reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity for homes, businesses, and communities across the province. We are energized to grow
, embracing opportunities to shape the future of a dynamic and evolving energy sector while advancing our careers. We are powered by teamwork
, supported by diverse and passionate colleagues who foster respect, celebrate successes, and thrive on shared achievements. At the IESO, it’s not just what we do— it’s who we are!

Who We Are

Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.

This is a non-unionized position that falls within the Corporate Relations, Engagement and Strategy business unit.

What Makes This Role Exciting

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

This is a unique opportunity to help shape the organization's strategic direction and drive initiatives that have enterprise-wide impact. Working closely with senior leaders, the role influences corporate strategy, oversees its implementation, and leads high-profile CEO and organizational priorities. The position offers a rare combination of strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and people leadership, allowing you to see ideas progress from concept to measurable results.

For someone who enjoys solving complex challenges and creating organizational alignment, this role sits at the center of the organization's most important priorities.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you’ll make a meaningful impact by contributing to the IESO team and supporting the electricity needs of the province through:

Leading the development and socialization of the Corporate Strategy, working in close partnership with Directors and senior leaders. Coordinate strategic planning activities, stakeholder engagement, and supporting research, and develop recommendations for Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and Board consideration and approval.
Leading the development of the Strategy Implementation Plan, including prioritization of strategic initiatives, milestones, performance measures, and implementation approaches. Facilitate engagement with business areas and provide recommendations to support ELT decision-making and approval.
Overseeing enterprise-wide monitoring, measurement, and reporting of progress against strategic objectives. Establish and implement reporting approaches, assess organizational performance against strategic commitments, identify emerging risks and issues, and provide insights and recommendations to support leadership decision-making.
Coordinating and aligning corporate strategy activities with other enterprise planning functions, including business planning, enterprise risk management, enterprise change, procurement, workforce planning, etc. Identify opportunities to strengthen the Enterprise Planning Framework and recommend improvements that enhance organizational alignment and execution.
Leading the delivery of CEO-sponsored and strategic initiatives, such as ESG framework, organizational alignment reviews, and other corporate priorities. Direct supporting research, analysis, and project activities; oversee external consultants and contractors where required; and develop recommendations arising from initiative outcomes for consideration by the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
Provide leadership, direction, and coaching to team members, ensuring the effective delivery of corporate strategy, strategy implementation planning, enterprise reporting, and strategic initiatives through clear priorities, performance expectations, and professional development support.

Decision-Making Responsibilities

Contribute to developing the approach, methodology, and stakeholder engagement process for the development of the Corporate Strategy and Strategy Implementation Plan.
Approve research, analysis, and other work products supporting strategy development, implementation planning, and strategic initiatives.
Determine the approach for strategy performance oversight and enterprise reporting.
Lead the selection and management of consultants and contractors supporting strategy or strategic initiative work, in accordance with organizational policies and procurement requirements.
Make decisions related to the coordination, prioritization, and execution of strategic and CEO-sponsored initiatives.

Recommendations

Recommend the Corporate Strategy, developed in collaboration with Directors and key stakeholders, for consideration and approval by the Executive Leadership Team and Board.
Recommend the Strategy Implementation Plan, including strategic priorities, sequencing of work, performance measures, and resource considerations, for Executive Leadership Team approval.
Recommend enhancements to the Enterprise Planning Framework to strengthen alignment across corporate strategy, business planning, enterprise risk management, enterprise change, workforce planning, procurement, and other enterprise functions.
Develop and present recommendations arising from CEO-sponsored and strategic initiatives, including opportunities, risks, implementation approaches, and organizational impacts, for consideration and approval by the CEO and Executive Leadership Team.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations to senior leadership on organizational performance, emerging issues, risks, trends, and opportunities identified through strategy oversight, reporting, and environmental scanning activities.

Role Requirements

Our team consists of experts from diverse backgrounds, each bringing their unique perspectives and skills.

To Succeed In This Role, You’ll Need

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Public Policy, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
12-15+ years of progressively senior experience in government relations, public affairs, strategy, policy, or a related function, preferably within the electricity or broader energy sector.
Strong knowledge of the electricity sector, government and regulatory environments, strategic planning and execution, business operations, and financial and budget management.
Proven ability to influence and build relationships with senior leaders, and other internal and external stakeholders.
Exceptional communication, presentation, and facilitation skills, with the ability to convey complex issues effectively and drive alignment.
Demonstrated success leading, developing, and motivating professional teams while fostering collaboration and delivering strategic outcomes.

How We Support You

From a comprehensive total rewards program to dynamic learning and development opportunities—including job rotations to broaden your expertise—we empower you to define and shape your own success. When you join the IESO, here’s what you can expect:

Best-in-class benefits and long-term support in the form of a defined benefit pension plan.
Work in a dynamic and evolving sector that offers exciting opportunities and the chance to explore new career paths.
Leadership that values meaningful discussions, welcomes feedback, and prioritizes career development.
A strong, inclusive culture and a collaborative team environment with a shared passion for impactful work.
Compensation packages that are regularly reviewed to remain competitive and to best accommodate the diverse needs of our employees.

Deadline

October 29, 2026. For future reference, please save a copy of the job posting as it will no longer be available once the posting closes.

Thank you for your interest in a career at the IESO. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Please note that the successful candidate must be legally eligible to work in Canada and will be subject to applicable background checks.

IESO will not conduct interviews or offer positions via online, text, chat or social media platforms. We will not gather personal information directly from candidates or potential candidates. Selected candidates will work with our Talent Acquisition team to ensure their application is processed.

The IESO currently has a 3-day in-office work week for applicable roles. Over the course of 2026, the IESO will advance plans to acquire additional office space to accommodate more in-office time. While the timeline for moving to a full 5-day in-office model has not yet been established, we are committed to keeping employees and candidates informed as plans progress and give them as much advance notice as possible to prepare for any changes.

We believe in opportunities for everyone.

At the IESO, we know that achieving great results depends on embracing diversity by attracting, developing, and retaining people from a wide variety of backgrounds. We do this by ensuring our recruitment and advancement policies are fair and equitable, and by creating an accessible and inclusive environment—one that values every team member’s unique skills and experiences and ensures they have the support they need to achieve their potential. If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please let us know. We’re proud to say we’ve been recognized as a supportive, inclusive employer.

Be sure to follow us on LinkedIn
